column1: # Lua-CDP Capstone column — PREDICTIONS, committed BEFORE the runs.
# The corpus is the 13 pure Lua<->C cross-domain-pointer use-after-frees in
# ../ (C++ and LuaJIT cases excluded — Capstone has no libc++/STL for
# capstone64, and LuaJIT has no capstone64 backend). Each row distills its
# case's memory lifecycle into a standalone shim (shims/<shim>.c) using the SAME
# revoke-on-free allocator, domain and host as the mruby column
# (../../capstone/), reused verbatim.
# Configs (as in ../../capstone/rows.tsv): Capstone has two that map onto CHERI's
# three:
#   bounds  = spatial only, no revocation   <-> CHERI "spatial"
#   revoke  = revoke-on-free                 <-> CHERI "eager"
# There is NO Capstone analogue of CHERI's async quarantine default — a fact
# about the mechanisms, reported not papered over. Only `revoke` is run here.
# Every row is a TEMPORAL cross-domain UAF by construction (that is what the
# corpus is), so every prediction is the same: the free that ends the native
# resource's life REVOKES it, and the stale access one crossing later FAULTS;
# the no-revoke control lets that access complete and reports MISS. The control
# is the discriminator — a FAULT whose control does not MISS is not attributable.
# fault_route: how the catch is expected to manifest under QEMU.
#   off0      the stale access is a plain load/store at offset 0 -> a clean
#             delivered cause-24/25 monitor fault (no pointer arithmetic).
#   interior  the access is at offset > 0 -> the interior address is formed by
#             cincoffset on the revoked capability, which hits QEMU's
#             assert-on-untagged gap (an emulator limitation, still scored FAULT;
#             see ../../capstone/ history 01-08-2026). Both count as prevented.
